Blocking finding CM-D1 — Specify the complete event acceptance state machine and trace-group conservation. In docs/phase2/cho51_p3_component_model_v1/capture-accounting.md:23–37 and62–72, the contract names mandatory transitions but does not define primary outcome cardinality or require PASS before a successful CASE_END. A HEADER followed by216 CASE_START/CASE_END(count=0) pairs and a FOOTER can satisfy the explicit start/end, sequence and no-negative-outcome checks while containing no PASS callbacks. qualification.md's all-started/completed/no-negative acceptance clauses do not close that gap. Define a successful case as exactly one primary PASS after its complete lifecycle, followed by one CASE_END, with no sticky negative case/subcase/fixture outcome; reject missing/duplicate or reordered primary outcomes and additional starts after failfast. Explicitly conserve multiple error/cleanup callbacks and failed-fixture/not-started cases without inventing completion. Also, count is null on failures and TRACE under the current table, so the verifier has no declared required TRACE cardinality: an omitted frame cannot be detected structurally. Bind each failure to a bounded exact frame count/group, require all corresponding ordered TRACE records and correct owner/ordinals, and specify zero-frame/nonexception routes. Add the negative transcript cases to the planned protocol contract tests and synchronize readiness/qualification semantics. This is one event-contract finding; no implementation or runtime defect is asserted.
